summary: The root "rbT" primarily means to tie or bind. It refers to horses kept tied, often for military readiness. The term also describes a monk or sage who restrains themselves from worldly pleasures.
lane: رَبِيطٌ ذ Tied, bound, or made fast; as also ; (K, TA;) applied to a horse, (Mgh,) or similar beast ( دَابَّة ); as also ; (TA;) applied to the former, i. q. مَرْبُوطٌ ; (Mgh;) or مَايُرْتَبَطُ [which may perhaps signify the same; but more probably, taken to be tied, or for keeping post, on the enemy's frontier ]; (S;) and [in like manner] رَبِيطَةٌ , applied to the latter, i. q. مَاٱرْتُبِطَ : (K:) and رَبِيطٌ applied to a horse also signifies tied and fed in the court of a house: (TA:) pl. رُبُطٌ (TA) and , (Mgh,) or the latter is a pl. pl., being pl. of رُبُطٌ . (TA.) مِنْ الخَيْلِ , in the Kur [viii. 62], means Of horses that are tied; (Bd, Mgh;) رِبَاطٌ being of the measure فِعَالٌ in the sense of the measure مَفْعولٌ ; or an inf. n. used as a subst., being an inf. n. of رَبَطَ in the sense of رَابَطَ ; (Bd;) or it is an inf. n. of رَابَطَ ; and therefore [when used as an epithet, like any inf. n. so used,] is applied to one as well as to a pl. number; (Ham p. 222;) or pl. of رَبِيطْ : (Bd, Mgh:) or it means of mares: (Fr, TA:) and رِبَاطٌ signifies horses; five thereof, and upwards: (S, K:) or horses, themselves, that are taken to be tied, or for keeping post, on the enemy's frontier. (L.) And you say, لِفُلَانٍ مِنَ الخَيْلِ Such a one has a stud constituting the source of his horses; like as you say تلَادٌ . (S.) , also, applied to horses, signifies Tied in a town or country or the like: occuring in a trad., in which it is said that upon every horse shall be levied a deenár; but upon the رابطة , nothing: properly meaning, in this case, ذَاتُ الرَّبْطِ ; being like رَاضِيَةٌ in the phrase عِيشَةٌ رَاضِيَةٌ . (Mgh.) -b2- See also رَابِطٌ . -b3- Also, and , (assumed tropical:) A monk: one who abstains from worldly pleasures: a sage who restrains himself from worldly things. (K, TA.) [In the L and TA, الرَّبِيطُ is also explained, as on the authority of Ez-Zejjájee, as signifying الذَّاهِبُ ; but this I think a mistranscription, for الرَّاهِبُ .] -A2- (assumed tropical:) Unripe dates soaked [ in water ]: (S, K:) or (assumed tropical:) fresh ripe dates soaked with water; also called مَنْقُوشٌ : (Sgh, TA in art. نقش :) or (tropical:) dried dates (A 'Obeyd, IF, A, K) put into jars ( جِرَار ), (A 'Obeyd, A,) and having water poured upon them, (A 'Obeyd, IF, K,) or moistened with water, in order that they may become like fresh ripe dates: (A:) but perhaps this is an adventitious term: (IF:) some say that it is رَبِيدٌ , and not original. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: He tied, bound; made fast; he tied

parts.t: (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) a thing, (S, Msb, * K, * TA,) and a beast; (Mgh, TA;) and in like manner
with a rope, in order that he might not run away.
Such a one ties so many head of beasts:
or the verb may here have a different signification, explained below]. (S, TA.) And it is said in a prov.,
Thou hast found a generous horse, therefore do thou preserve him;
: relating to the duty of preservation. (TA.) See also 3.

headwords.def: رَبَطَ , (S, Mgh, &c.,) aor. رَبِطَ and رَبُطَ , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. رَبْطٌ , (Msb, TA,) He tied, bound, or made fast, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) a thing, (S, Msb, * K, * TA,) and a beast; (Mgh, TA;) and in like manner he tied, or bound, a beast with a rope, in order that he might not run away. (TA.) You say, فُلَانٌ كَذَا رَأْسًا مِنَ الدَّوَابِّ [ Such a one ties so many head of beasts: or the verb may here have a different signification, explained below]. (S, TA.) And it is said in a prov., اِسْتَكْرَمْتَ فَٱرْبِطْ , or, accord. to one relation, أَكْرَمْتَ , i. e. Thou hast found a generous horse, therefore do thou preserve him; or, as some relate it, : relating to the duty of preservation. (TA.) See also 3. رَبَطَ عَلَيْهِ (assumed tropical:)

headwords.def: المُرَابَطَةُ signifies, (K, TA,) in its primary acceptation, (TA,) Two [ hostile ] parties' tying of their horses, each at their frontier, and each in preparation for the other: (K, TA:) and رِبَاطُ الخَيْلِ and مُرَابَطَتُهَا signify the same [as above]. (S, TA.) [You say, رَابَطَ الفَرِيقَانِ The two parties tied their horses at their respective frontiers, each in preparation for the other. ] And one says, with reference to horses, , inf. n. رَبْطٌ and رِبَاطٌ , as well as رابط , inf. n. مُرَابَطَةٌ and رِبَاطٌ . (Bd in viii. 62.) Hence, (Sgh, L, K,) رابط , (Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. رِبَاطٌ (S, Mgh, Sgh, L, K) and مُرَابَطَةٌ , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He, or it, (an army, Mgh) kept post, or remained, on, or at, the frontier (S, Mgh, Sgh, L, K)

headwords.gloss: He took a horse for the purpose of tying him; keeping post, on the enemy's frontier; He

headwords.def: إِرْتَبَطَ see 1, in three places. ارتبط فَرَسًا He took a horse for the purpose of tying him, or keeping post, on the enemy's frontier. (K, * TA.) [ He, or it, became tied, bound, or made fast. ] ارتبط فِى الحَبْلِ He became caught, or entangled, in the rope. (Lh.) اِرْتِبَاطٌ is also explained by AO and Ez-Zejjájee as syn. with اعْتلَاقٌ . (TA.) [Thus, ارتبطهُ signifies He, or it, attached himself, or itself, or clung, or clave, to him, or it: (see a citation from Lebeed, voce بَعْضٌ :) and app. also (assumed tropical:) he loved him. ]

headwords.def: رِبَاطٌ A thing with which one ties, binds, or makes fast, (S, Msb, K,) a skin, (S, Msb,) and a beast, (S,) &c.; (S, Msb;) a rope with which a beast is tied: (Mgh:) pl. رُبُطٌ (S, Msb, K) and رُبْطٌ ; (S, TA;) the latter a contraction of the former: (TA:) and and also signify a thing with which a beast is tied. (K.) It is said in a prov., إِنْ ذَهَبَ عَيْرٌ فَعَيْرٌ فِى الرِّبَاطِ [ If an ass is gone away, an ass is tied to the cord ]: relating to contentment with what is present and relinquishment of what is absent. (Mgh.) [See also 3.] [Hence,] used by the vulgar in the sense of أُخْذَةٌ , meaning (assumed tropical:) A kind of fascination by which enchantresses withhold their husbands from other women. (TA in art. اخذ .)

headwords.def: رَابِطٌ [act. part. n. of 1]. خَلَّفَ فُلَانٌ بِالثَّغْرِ جَيْشًا رَابِطَةً [ Such a one left behind him on the frontier an army having their horses tied in preparation for the enemy; or keeping post ]. (S.) And بِبَلَدِ كَذَا رَابِطَةٌ مِنَ الخَيْلِ [ In such a town, or country, or the like, is a company of horsemen having their horses tied at the frontier in preparation for the enemy; or keeping post on the frontier: or it may perhaps mean, a number of horses tied: see رَبِيطٌ ]. (S.) also signifies A company of warriors; or of men warring against an enemy: (Mgh:) or a company of men having their horses tied at the frontier in preparation for the enemy; or keeping post on the frontier; and in like manner [its pl.] مُرَابِطَاتٌ
